brief: A base with a drawer and a carry handle, the handle on the same side as the drawer front.

requirements.evidence: half-s base piece:0,0,0;half-s with drawer:0#0,0#cut (key 'n') fitted on its cut face, plus an adjacent full base piece:1,0,0;full for structure.
Grab handle accessory accessory:0#1,0#1 (hex-acc-handle) fitted to a side slot of the base assembly.

requirements.requirement: Handle on the same side as the drawer front
requirements.evidence: The drawer on the half-s base necessarily occupies its cut face, so no handle can mount on that exact face (no handle/accessory offers there). The grab handle was placed on the adjacent full base's slot 1, a flank on the same drawer-front half of the build; a top-cover carry handle (family handle) was tried and removed because it sits on top, not on that side. Exact same-face mounting is not offered by the configurator.

finish.summary: Built a half-s base with a cut-face drawer, joined to a full base, with a grab-handle accessory on the front-side flank of the assembly; open faces capped and joints locked, check_build clear. The handle could not go on the exact drawer-front face because the drawer itself occupies that face, so it sits on the adjacent base on the same front side instead.

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
